title: Pell Moves Out
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: Theo's imaginary friend is moving out tonight.
first_visual: A tiny cardboard suitcase on a child's floor, packed with crayons and one sock.

beats.visual: A tiny cardboard suitcase on Theo's floor; the lid snaps shut.
beats.vo: Theo's imaginary friend is moving out tonight.

beats.visual: Theo holds up a crayon drawing of a tall thin figure waving.
beats.vo: Pell. Lived under his bed since summer.

beats.visual: Theo: 'He found someone with more room.' Ivy: 'Another kid?' Theo shakes his head.
Night: Ivy in bed; the suitcase at the foot of the bed, lid open, empty.
beats.vo: That night the suitcase was by my bed. Empty.

beats.visual: Key moment: Ivy's shadow on the wall grows a second thin head that turns to look at her.
Theo in the lit doorway, small; moth on his pyjamas.

ending: Theo in the doorway: 'He says thank you.'
loop_note: No. It ends on a quiet line that invites comments.

originality_review: Original. 'The imaginary friend leaves the child for an adult' reverses the usual 'imaginary friend is real' trope. Pell is our own invented name and character.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Theo's imaginary friend Pell packs a tiny suitcase to move out. He has found somewhere roomier: Ivy.

hooks.line: Theo's imaginary friend is moving out tonight.
hooks.first_visual: A tiny cardboard suitcase on a child's floor, packed with crayons and one sock.

hooks.line: I was relieved his imaginary friend was leaving.
hooks.first_visual: A crayon drawing of a tall thin figure waving goodbye.

hooks.line: 'He found someone with more room,' Theo said.
hooks.first_visual: A boy pointing up at an adult, off-frame.

hooks.line: The suitcase was at the foot of my bed. Empty.
hooks.first_visual: An open, empty little suitcase on a dark floor.

hooks.line: My shadow has two heads now.
hooks.first_visual: A shadow on a bedroom wall with a second thin head on its shoulder.

setting: Theo's bedroom, then Ivy's bedroom (the same E3 room, redressed).
conflict: Ivy is glad the 'friend' is leaving, until she learns where he is going.
escalation: The suitcase, the drawing, then Theo's pointing finger.
reveal: That night the empty suitcase is beside Ivy's bed, and her shadow has a second, thinner head.
emotional_objective: Childlike sweetness inverted into possession dread.
